title: Avoid repeated linear list searches
why: Calling count or index on a list scans it linearly, so repeating the search in a loop can make the surrounding operation quadratic.
suggestion: Precompute counts or indexes, or use a set or dictionary when repeated lookup is the intended operation.
limitations: Only count and index calls on variables explicitly annotated as lists or initialized with a list expression are reported inside tracked loops.
A search immediately followed by a same-scope break is accepted; mutation, reassignment, and exact loop bounds are not inferred.
